title: qos golden re-bless now pins a same-tick resolve+re-trigger cycle — two Crisis_Triggered events for the single surge activation, undisclosed by the W4 change-log
evidence: core/crisis.odin:74-75: "// pins: a persistent flaw emits ONE trigger per activation [E13]."; spec-4-2-surge-crisis.md:162: "    qos.dem's trigger element changed (bundle 0 vs the blessed bundle 1) — T1/log/T2 re-blessed,"; goldens/qos.t1 (r1 b94d54f vs r2 f906725): "-1200 ca44329e929c4dbb" → "+1200 6124c5b772c0aa7b" (ticks 1200-1500 all shifted). Decoded serialized-state dumps (harness run of both shas, qos demo): r1 tick 1200 event payload "08000101000100000001000000 ... target= 1 pipe= 1"; r2 tick 1200 "08000101000000000000000000 ... target= 0 pipe= 0"; r2 tick 1201 tail: "event @0x779: RESOLVED arch=0 cause=1 class=1 target=0 pipe=0" + "event @0x78e: TRIGGERED arch=0 cause=1 class=1 target=1 pipe=1"; r2 crisis row at ticks 1300/1500: "bundle=1 pipe=1 class=1 mult=10 triggered=1201" (r1: "triggered=1200").
detail: The W4 attribution change made qos trigger on bundle 0 at 1200, resolve it at 1201 while the surge still saturates the map (bundle 1 sheds class-1 every tick), then re-trigger same tick on bundle 1 — the E13 chatter pattern the hysteresis comments claim to prevent, now pinned in the blessed golden.
recommended_fix: Disclose the resolve+re-trigger cycle in the change-log and pin a no-chatter contract (one trigger per activation under a steady surge), or make the engine hold the activation's element until the named flaw is genuinely relieved.

title: spec-4-2 change-log claims qos 'T1/log/T2 re-blessed' — only goldens/qos.t1 moved in the rework
